newsitem.title: UK: Shoppers denied gene product choice, UK group says.
newsitem.headline: Shoppers denied gene product choice, UK group says.

text.p: British consumers are being denied the choice of whether or not to eat genetically modified (GM) products, Britain's Consumer Association said in its publication "Which?".

Shoppers do not know what they are buying because retailers say they are not told by food suppliers whether the modified crops have been used, "Which?" said. This means GM products cannot be labelled as such.

"Not one major supermarket chain or food manufacturer out of 60 could guarantee that it would label products containing GM strains of two widely used ingredients - maize and soya - when quizzed by Which? last November," the magazine said.
"Supermarkets say they can't label their products accurately because GM maize and GM soya is being mixed with standard crops by US suppliers," it said.
"There's no proof that genetic modification poses a risk to health, and it is argued that it can improve some foods," according to Andrew McIlwraith, Which? senior editor.
"But consumers should have the right to avoid GM foods if they want to. All foods containing GM ingredients should be clearly and accurately labelled."
The European Commission plans to issue guidelines to EU member states by mid-March on the labelling of genetically modified food, the Commission's environment spokesman said on Wednesday.
In December, the European Commission approved a French request to authorise imports from the U.S. of gene-maize developed by the Swiss firm Ciba Geigy AG.
In March, the Commission approved imports of modified soybeans from the U.S. that had been genetically altered by Monsanto Co to make them resistant to a herbicide.
